log.what: experimental baseline of the existing Darwin/AArch64 M19ef worker bridge on the hosted macos runner (check darwin-worker-baseline, non-required, not parity evidence)
log.result: PASS on hosted macOS ARM64: builder compiled natively (11.9 s); 7 worker cases linked, signed and run 8 times each with exact output
log.conclusion: the internal bridge works on hosted hardware with 2 worker slots; it is not the public API and not parity

log.what: generalise the Darwin ARM64 worker bridge from 2 to 16 slots (PR #79 commit 074adc5), new 12-worker case under GC stress
log.result: hosted macos-15 ARM64, run 42981455254: all 7 original cases still PASS x8; the 12 concurrent workers computed the correct total 3914700; the only mismatch was the test's own expectation of the collect return value (live bytes, 240, not 0)
findings: the bridge writes a 360-byte binary evidence record to stderr at shutdown: the public mode must not do this
bridge assembler/Mach-O bounds (4096/8192/10244 words) had to be raised together to link more than 3 contexts

log.what: public start/join on darwin-arm64: build pipeline routes thread programs through the cooperative worker bridge (PR #79 commit da3d54c)
log.result: hosted macos-15 ARM64, run 42996933167: check darwin-thread-core PASS (tests/threads/core_runtime.mio built by the native CLI, run 10x normal and 10x --gc-stress, exact output); darwin-worker-baseline PASS for all 8 cases incl. 12 concurrent workers under GC stress
log.limits: start and join only: no word natives, no kiso/thread, no channels, join of an invalid handle traps, at most 16 live threads (a 17th start is a runtime error); cells I/J/K stay UNSUPPORTED
log.follow_up: the stale thread-natives-fail-closed check failed on darwin-arm64 because threads now run there: it is replaced on that target by thread-channels-fail-closed (channel programs must still be rejected)

log.what: word natives and kiso/thread channels on darwin-arm64 (PR #79 commit d940944)
log.result: hosted macos-15 ARM64, run 43002395379: darwin-thread-programs 11 of 12 cases PASS (basic, captures, many, channel_basic, channel_close, channel_graphs, channel_mpmc, summary_copy normal; basic, channel_basic, channel_close under --gc-stress); nested FAIL (exit 1: threads started or joined from a non-main thread hit runtime_error); thread-invalid-handles-fail-closed PASS
log.limits: start/join only from the main thread; no join_status/join_checked; no generation-checked handles; word_wait polls with a 50us timed sleep; 16 live threads; 16384 channels per process; not yet run: gc_stress, reclaim, lifecycle, creation_limit, shutdown, races, faults, negatives; cells I/J/K stay UNSUPPORTED until these pass
log.next: allow nested start/join (slot allocation lock), then join_status and generation handles, then the remaining tests/threads programs

log.what: darwin-arm64 cells I, J and K validated (PRs #79, #89, #91, #92 merged)
log.result: run 43166577034 head c5b3b54: all thread, channel, fault and ownership programs pass natively; 128 live threads; the failures found on the way (channel wait starvation, 1000-entry root snapshot overflow, main-thread-only start/join, shutdown join) are fixed and recorded in the PRs
log.limits: 128 live threads (4096 on linux-amd64) and a start beyond that returns -11; 16384 channel control blocks per process; each thread image is about 6.5 MB (the runtime area is stored in the file); word_wait is a bounded spin then an exponential-backoff sleep up to 20 ms, not a park; a thread stack overflow ends with the runtime's controlled error (exit 1) where Linux dies by SIGSEGV; OS calls other than join and the word natives are not safepoint-aware in a thread; stress runs do not prove race freedom
log.next: linux-arm64 threads (futex-free park protocol, polls, thread natives in the AArch64 lowering), then darwin-amd64, windows-amd64, windows-arm64
